To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we solved the crystal structure of the Arabidopsis thalia glutamate-1- semialdehyde-2.1-aminomutasase (GSAM), which is an enzyme involved in the biosynthesis of tetrapyrrole compounds, and that the structure shows asymmetry in cofactors binding as well as asymmetry in the gating loop orientation.

the structure of the Arabidopsis thalia GSAM enzyme is asymmetric in cofactor binding and in the gating-loop position, which supports the previous hypothesis of negative cooperativity between the monomers of GSMA.

The crystal structures of the Arabidopsis thalanina glutamate-1- semialdehyde-2-1-aminomutasae in the apo form and in complex with the reaction product, 5-aminolevulinate, were determined at resolutions of 2.0 and 2.2 Å, respectively.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the GSAM enzyme is a dimeric protein that contains one FAD and one PLP per monomer and one PLP cofactor in each dimer.
the structure of GSAM is not a simple dimer of the monomer but a complex of two monomers with a different orientation of the gating loop.
there is no clear consensus on the role of GSAM in the regulation of the tetrapyrrole pathway, but that there are some indications for the presence of a regulatory role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystal structures of GSAM have provided a detailed view of a complex enzyme, and that the structural information has been useful in interpreting the biochemical results.
the structural and functional properties of GSAM have been elucidated in a way that provides the foundation for further research in this important enzyme.
the crystal structure provides an atomic-level understanding of the catalytic mechanism of GSAM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GSAM is a unique member of the family of radical SAM enzymes and that the structural features of GSAM are consistent with the proposed mechanism of the enzyme.
the gating-loop orientation is a key determinant of the substrate binding mode in GSAM.
the structural asymmetry in GSAM is likely the cause of the previously observed negative cooperativity.
